ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a flip-flop block labeled FF, the upper-left input terminal is labeled T, and this terminal is connected to fixed logic “1”; there is also a CP pulse input on the left connected to the clock terminal of the flip-flop; the output terminal on the right is labeled Q, and another output with an inversion mark is Q̄. Reasoning: This circuit can be identified as a T flip-flop, and T=1. When T=1, the T flip-flop toggles the output Q once for every CP pulse, so Q needs two CP pulses to complete one full cycle, and the output frequency is half of the input clock frequency. Given that the CP frequency is 4 kHz, the frequency of Q = 4/2 = 2 kHz.

method.method_draft: Use the image to establish that the flip-flop has T=1 and is clocked by CP. Apply the T-FF state equation: with T=1, each CP pulse changes Q to its opposite state. Starting from either initial state, Q alternates 0,1,0,1,... or 1,0,1,0,..., so two CP pulses are needed to return Q to the same state. Thus the output period is twice the CP period, giving f_Q = 4 kHz / 2 = 2 kHz.
